verdicts.tldr: a screenshot that shows an error page or a page that never painted is published as the realm's rendering
verdicts.details: shots.go:187-189 is the whole post-run health check: `if fi, err := os.Stat(out); err != nil || fi.Size() == 0 { return fmt.Errorf("chrome wrote no image") }`. It stats the destination path, not anything this run produced, and it asks nothing about what was rendered. The snapshot is served by http.FileServer (shots.go:159), which answers a miss with a plain-text `404 page not found` body that Chrome paints and screenshots at exit 0, so chromeShot returns nil and ScreenshotPairs sets pair.After at shots.go:83; comment.go:121 then captions that image `after - this PR`. Fix: assert the run wrote the file this invocation (stat before, compare mtime or write to a fresh temp path) and check the HTTP status of the URL before shooting it.
verdicts.evidence: read at head: shots.go:184-190, the only check after cmd.CombinedOutput is os.Stat(out)+Size()==0; no status check, no content check, no per-run freshness check. shots.go:159 Handler: http.FileServer(http.Dir(dir)). The byte-identical slow/blank digests (slow=2bff94039a8c blank=2bff94039a8c) are the finder's Chrome 152 measurement, not rerun here; the missing-check mechanism is settled by the read alone.
verdicts.verify_by: tests/b4-lines-r2-chromeshot-silent-truncation_test.go: copy into misc/gnopreview and run go test -run TestB4ChromeShotSilentTruncation -v ./...

verdicts.tldr: every over-budget source page is still rendered in full by gnodev and then thrown away, so the file budget costs render time it does not save
verdicts.details: Run fetches before it charges: crawl.go:129 `body, code, err := c.getRetry(u)`, then the 200 check, then crawl.go:138 `if !c.chargeFile(u) { ... continue }`. wantFile at crawl.go:231 reads `c.fileBudget[realm] < c.FileBudget`, a counter only chargeFile advances, and it is consulted at link-enqueue time (crawl.go:148-150), so a $source overview that links N files queues all N in one burst before any capture has charged a slot. Each is then fetched whole from gnodev, chroma highlighting included, and dropped. Fix: re-test the budget at dequeue time, before getRetry, and keep chargeFile for the capture that survives.
verdicts.evidence: read at head: crawl.go:129-141 orders getRetry, the status check, chargeFile in that sequence; crawl.go:231 `return c.fileBudget[realm] < c.FileBudget`; crawl_test.go:304-315 TestFileBudgetChargedOnCaptureNotDiscovery asserts inScope returns true five times under FileBudget 1, pinning the unbounded-discovery behaviour rather than bounding it. The 12-request count was not run here.
verdicts.verify_by: read Run lines 129-141 against wantFile line 231, then crawl_test.go:309-313; count requests from an httptest $source page linking 12 file= URLs under FileBudget 2

verdicts.tldr: the before pass reuses the head's assets on purpose, and the code and the README both say so
verdicts.details: The read reproduces the mechanism exactly as filed - main.go:274 `base.Write(cfg.out, "")`, crawl.go:304 `if assets == "" { return c.writePages(dir) }`, and the ../ depth from _before/ resolving into the single head-populated <out>/public - but it is the stated contract, not an oversight. ScreenshotPairs' own doc says both passes use the same gnoweb so the pair shows the realm change and nothing else, and README.md:60-62 repeats it. A pair rendered against two different asset trees would confound the realm diff with a chrome diff, which is what the design rules out. Fix: none on this line; the residual gap is that main.go:147-150 is an if/else, so a PR changing gnoweb frontend and a realm together takes the pairs branch and gets no gnoweb chrome sample at all - a different claim from the one filed.
verdicts.evidence: proving lines, shots.go:47-49: "Both passes use the SAME gnoweb - the binary and the assets come from the head - so what the pair shows is the realm change and nothing else." README.md:60-62: "Both passes run the head's gnodev and reference the head's assets, so the pair differs by the realm change and nothing else."
verdicts.refuted_by: shots.go:47-49 "Both passes use the SAME gnoweb - the binary and the assets come from the head - so what the pair shows is the realm change and nothing else."
verdicts.verify_by: read crawl.go:303-306 and crawl.go:348-362, then render a branch carrying both a gnoweb css change and a realm change

verdicts.tldr: one oversized realm render can take the whole preview job down, since nothing bounds bytes and every captured body stays in memory to the end
verdicts.details: crawl.go:444 is `b, err := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)` with no wrapper, and a grep for LimitReader, MaxBytes, ContentLength, maxBody, maxSize and max-size across every .go file in misc/gnopreview returns nothing. Each body is stored whole at crawl.go:143 `p := &page{... Body: body}` into c.pages and freed by nothing before Write, so peak memory is page count times page size with only the count capped. README.md's Bounds section (line 106 onward) offers -max-pages as its one quantitative lever and otherwise excludes shapes by weight. Fix: wrap the body in an io.LimitReader at a documented cap, count bytes against a total budget alongside MaxPages, and say in Bounds what the byte cap is.
verdicts.evidence: grep -rnE 'LimitReader|MaxBytes|ContentLength|maxBody|max-size|maxSize' misc/gnopreview/*.go -> NONE. crawl.go:443-445 reads the body whole with only the 30s client Timeout above it. Heap was not measured here.
verdicts.verify_by: grep -n 'LimitReader|MaxBytes|maxBody|ContentLength' crawl.go main.go (empty), then grep -i 'cap|size|limit' README.md to read what Bounds claims

verdicts.tldr: a realm path that moves drops one sample shot from the comment with nothing said on stderr
verdicts.details: plan.go:37-42 lists the four seed realms and shots.go:107-112 re-types three of them as raw URLs (home, home$source, boards2/v0$help, docs/security_patterns); blog is a seed with no shot and no symbol is shared between the two lists. The lookup at shots.go:134 `p, ok := c.pages[canonicalURL(s.url)]` falls to `if !ok { continue }` at line 135, which is the one failure path in Screenshot that prints nothing - the chromeShot failure just below it prints `! screenshot %s`. A rename in examples/, a dropped seed, or plan.go:265's `pkgs[r] != nil` guard skipping one then ships a three-image grid where four were intended, and the render log looks clean. Fix: derive shotPlan's realm paths from gnowebSeedRealms (or assert the correspondence in a test) and log the skip on stderr.

The finder's mutation run (boards2/v0 -> v1) went red as expected.

verdicts.tldr: a full merge-base render of every changed realm is committed to the shared previews site where no link, index entry or reader reaches it
verdicts.details: main.go:265 gives the base crawler `Prefix: beforeDir` and main.go:274 `base.Write(cfg.out, "")` writes one page per changed realm that exists at the merge base into <out>/_before/. Only maxPairs=2 of them are ever read, by Chrome, as PNGs; pr-preview-publish.yml:140 then `cp -r ../_preview/. "pr-$PR/"` commits the whole tree and line 128 measures it against MAX_PREVIEW_MIB=40. beforeDir is also declared in shots.go, the screenshot file, and read only from main.go - it names the base crawl, not a shot. Fix: write _before/ only for the realms that get a pair, or link the tree from the comment so the bytes buy something; move beforeDir beside the crawl that uses it.
verdicts.evidence: grep -rn '_before|beforeDir' misc/gnopreview/*.go -> main.go:224 (doc), main.go:265 (Prefix), crawl.go:54 (doc), shots.go:26-27 (doc + const). No reader anywhere in comment.go or plan.go. publish.yml:138-140 rm -rf / mkdir -p / cp -r of the whole snapshot. Same underlying fact as candidates 210 and 217, framed as placement plus published weight.

verdicts.tldr: every published path starts with an underscore, so the preview's images and tab pages survive only on a marker file this PR never writes
verdicts.details: shotsDir is `_shots` (shots.go:24) and the tab and render-argument directories are `_t`/`_a`, so a Jekyll build on the previews site drops all of them. A grep for nojekyll across misc/gnopreview and .github/workflows returns exactly one hit, README.md:96, which states the marker is mandatory wherever the site is published - a prose dependency on an out-of-tree manual step, with no workflow step writing it and none checking it. If the previews repo is ever recreated, forked or re-pointed without it, every in every sticky comment 404s while the render and publish jobs stay green. Fix: `touch .nojekyll` in the publish job before `git add -A`, which is idempotent and removes the dependency.
verdicts.evidence: grep -rni nojekyll over misc/gnopreview and .github/workflows -> misc/gnopreview/README.md:96 only. pr-preview-publish.yml:138-141 does rm -rf / mkdir -p / cp -r / git add -A and writes no dotfile. Whether gnolang/gno-previews carries the marker today was not checked - it is out of this tree.
verdicts.verify_by: grep -rn nojekyll over the PR (ran: one README hit); then curl -sI <previews site>/pr-<N>/_shots/<name>.png and git ls-files .nojekyll in the previews repo

verdicts.tldr: the reviewer cannot open the before page the README promises, and pays for it in the 40 MiB preview budget
verdicts.details: comment.go:117-119 renders the before cell as a bare `` while comment.go:120-121 wraps only the after image in ``, and the href it uses is p.URL, which shots.go:77 fills with `path.Dir(afterFile) + "/"` - the after page. Index() at comment.go:166-177 iterates p.Realms against the head crawler's c.pages, so no _before entry appears there either, and ShotPair (shots.go:34-44) carries no field for the before page at all. README.md:73-74 says _before/ exists "so a reviewer can click through to the before page and not just its screenshot", which nothing in the generated output makes possible. Fix: add a BeforeURL field to ShotPair, fill it from path.Dir(beforeFile), and wrap the before cell's img in that href.

verdicts.tldr: every closed PR keeps a permanent comment of broken image boxes, and no job can repair it
verdicts.details: comment.go:90 writes the footer "Rebuilt on every push to this PR; removed when PR #%s closes", and pr-preview-cleanup.yml does exactly that with `rm -rf "pr-$PR"` as its only mutation. Every that pairGrid (comment.go:118, 121) and shotGrid (comment.go:141) wrote then 404s in the PR's permanent history. The cleanup job carries `permissions: {}` at both the workflow and the job level and holds only the previews deploy key; grep -c 'gh api' over that file returns 0, so it cannot rewrite the comment it invalidates. Fix: have the cleanup job PATCH the sticky comment down to a one-line 'preview removed' note, which needs `issues: write` and the marker lookup the publish job already implements.
verdicts.evidence: read of .github/workflows/pr-preview-cleanup.yml whole: `permissions: {}` twice (workflow and job), the Remove pr-<N> step's only mutation is `rm -rf "pr-$PR"`, and grep -c 'gh api' -> 0. Footer at comment.go:90.
verdicts.verify_by: read .github/workflows/pr-preview-cleanup.yml for permissions, rm -rf, and any gh api call

verdicts.tldr: the reviewer may read a before/after belonging to the previous push, with nothing in the comment saying so
verdicts.details: The two halves the read can settle both hold: shots.go:76 `name := slug(strings.TrimPrefix(urlOf(r), "/"))` makes the shot filename a pure function of the realm path, the publish job writes it under a per-PR directory whose URL carries no sha (pr-preview-publish.yml:138-140), and the comment is edited in place at pr-preview-publish.yml:174 `gh api -X PATCH "repos/$REPO/issues/comments/$id"`. So a second push republishes new bytes at a byte-identical URL inside an unchanged comment body. Whether GitHub's image proxy then serves the previous push's PNG depends on its cache TTL, which cannot be read from this tree - that half is unverified here. Fix: put the head sha in the shot filename, or append it as a query string in the comment's img src, so each push addresses its own image.
verdicts.evidence: read at head: shots.go:76 (filename from the realm path alone), pr-preview-publish.yml:138-140 (rm -rf/mkdir/cp into pr-$PR) and :174 (PATCH of the existing comment id). No live push or cache-header check was possible from the worktree.
verdicts.verify_by: push twice to a PR inside the cache window and compare the image GitHub renders against _preview/_shots/*.png; curl -I the published PNG and read its Cache-Control

verdicts.tldr: when the 1280x860 shot crops what changed, the reviewer has no way to read the before page's text
verdicts.details: ShotPair carries one page URL and shots.go:77 fills it with the after page only: `pair := ShotPair{Realm: r, URL: path.Dir(afterFile) + "/", New: newRealms[r]}`. ScreenshotPairs computes beforeFile at shots.go:89, uses it for the screenshot, and discards it; comment.go:118 emits the before cell as a bare img while 121 wraps the after one in an href, and Index() emits nothing under _before/. The published tree therefore carries a whole merge-base render that no generated link reaches, against README.md:73-74's statement that it exists for exactly that click-through. Fix: keep beforeFile on ShotPair and wrap the before cell in its href, the same shape the after cell already uses. The candidate anchors shots.go:86, which is the "New in this PR" comment; the line that sets URL is 77.

verdicts.tldr: a page the preview server cannot find is photographed and captioned as the realm, with nothing on stderr
verdicts.details: chromeShot's only verdict is shots.go:187-189, a non-empty file at the destination, so a URL the snapshot server answers 404 on returns nil: http.FileServer (shots.go:159) sends a plain-text `404 page not found` body, Chrome paints it, exits 0 and writes a real PNG. ScreenshotPairs at shots.go:78-83 then sets pair.After and the comment captions that error page as the realm. Today every afterFile comes from head.FileOf over c.pages, whose pages writePages has written, so the miss is latent rather than live - it goes live the first time a page's file name and its served path stop agreeing, through a prefix, an escape or a writeFile that failed. Fix: HEAD the URL and fail the shot on a non-200 before invoking Chrome.
verdicts.evidence: read at head: shots.go:186-190 is the whole check; shots.go:157-163 serve() hands the directory to http.FileServer, whose miss is a 200-shaped page to a browser. The finder's run recorded `chromeShot on a URL the server answers 404 on returned nil and wrote 6743 bytes`; the mechanism is settled by the read without it.
verdicts.verify_by: go test -run TestChromeShotFalseSuccess/missing_page ./... in misc/gnopreview with the artifact test
